topics.topic: Security-review status of A21 after the A01 concurrency amendment
questions: Was the security review reopened and performed again for A01's new create-versus-anonymisation/erasure concurrency rule, or is A21 now pending review?
Is A21 reopened and awaiting a new accepted security review of the amended A01, or was that review re-performed so A21 may remain closed?

judgement.why: A01 changed after closure, so the reopening rule makes the review open while the unchanged completeness claim says it remains complete.

witness.initial: A21 declares its security review complete and names A01 in the concurrency category.
events: The accepted A01 rules are amended to serialize creates against anonymisation or erasure.
A release reviewer determines whether the security review is currently complete.
outcomes: Applying the reopening rule, A21 is open and the release reviewer requires another security review.
Applying the completeness claim, A21 remains complete and the release reviewer proceeds without another review.
witness.observer: The release reviewer deciding whether States 0–2 have a completed security review.
basis: A create and the anonymisation or erasure that removes its request id are applied one at a time too, each on the result of the one before: a repeat applied before it answers the record as rule 4 says, one applied after it is a new create (rule 8).

topics.topic: Post-anonymisation create replay behavior and applicability of current refusal conditions
questions: After anonymisation removes the original request id, is repeating the create guaranteed to make and return a new record, or may current create refusal conditions prevent it?

quotes: Erasing a customer or anonymising a project removes everything that would tell a repeat (R0-06, R0-62); a create repeated after that is a new create, and its answer shows the new record it made.

A request id leaves its record with the values anonymisation or erasure removes (M01, M04); a create arriving after that with the same request id is a new create, checked as any create — a customer it names that is now restricted, ended or erased refuses it — and, when accepted, answered with the new record it made, so it is not silent (R0-36, owner, 2026-11-01).
judgement.why: State 0 unconditionally says the repeated create makes and answers a new record, while A01 permits current create conditions to refuse it without making one.

bases.passage: Erasing a customer or anonymising a project removes everything that would tell a repeat (R0-06, R0-62); a create repeated after that is a new create, and its answer shows the new record it made.

witness.initial: An archived project P was created with request id K, names an unrestricted customer C, and still keeps its values.
events: The owner anonymises P, removing its request id and customer link.
The owner repeats P's original create using request id K and naming C.
outcomes: State 0 makes a new project and answers it.
A01 refuses the new create because C is now restricted and makes no project.
witness.observer: The owner, who receives either a new project or a refusal.
basis: The owner restricts a customer's processing and may lift the restriction where a lawful ground allows it.
